subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What should OpenClaw do when a required exec-backed SecretRef fails during gateway startup under a process supervisor?
rationale: Changing startup from immediate fail-fast to retry, degrade, pause, or cache affects credential availability, rate-limit safety, and fail-closed security behavior, so automation should not pick the permanent policy alone.

options.title: Focused generic startup retry policy
options.body: Add bounded, provider-agnostic startup retry/backoff and clear operator guidance in `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts`, while still failing closed for persistent required-secret failures.

options.title: External resolver/plugin handoff
options.body: Keep core startup fail-fast and steer rate-limit/caching behavior to ClawHub resolver plugins such as Varlock, accepting that supervised core startup can still amplify provider failures.

options.title: Configurable retry/circuit breaker
options.body: Add a new documented SecretRef retry or circuit-breaker config surface with upgrade-safe defaults and tests, accepting the added configuration contract.

recommendation.title: Focused generic startup retry policy
recommendation.body: Add bounded, provider-agnostic startup retry/backoff and clear operator guidance in `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts`, while still failing closed for persistent required-secret failures.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest feature-history signal for the SecretRef runtime/schema behavior that the policy would change.
